description: Fig. 3 is a single 3D surface plot (MATLAB-style rendering) built from six stacked horizontal planes, each at a fixed value of the DRX fraction φ_d^(I) on the vertical axis, whose ticks are 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1. The two in-plane horizontal axes are ln Z_p^(I) on the front-right edge (ticks 22, 24, 26, 28, 30, 32, 34, 36) and ln Z_p^(II)(ε+Δε) on the front-left edge (same tick values but drawn 36 down to 22); both are dimensionless. Surface colour encodes the stress softening coefficient k_s(ε+Δε) through the colour bar at the right, which runs from dark blue at 0.2 through green to bright yellow at 1, with printed ticks 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1. The bottom plane (φ_d^(I) = 0) is uniformly bright yellow, i.e. k_s = 1. The upper planes stay yellow along the diagonal where the stage-I and stage-II ln Z_p values coincide and grade to green and blue at the corners where the two Zener–Hollomon parameters differ most. The figure therefore demonstrates that the softening effect on the saturation stress, expressed as the decline of k_s below 1, strengthens both with increasing mismatch between the two stages' Z_p and with rising stage-I DRX fraction. No individual data points or numeric values are printed on the surface.

subfigures.description: Single unlabelled 3D surface plot: six stacked horizontal planes at φ_d^(I) = 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1, with in-plane axes ln Z_p^(I) (22-36) and ln Z_p^(II)(ε+Δε) (22-36). Colour encodes k_s(ε+Δε) per the right-hand colour bar (0.2-1). Lowest plane is uniformly yellow (k_s = 1); upper planes turn green/blue at corners of largest Z_p mismatch.

observations.observation: The figure is a single 3D stacked-plane surface plot with no lettered sub-panels.
The vertical axis is labelled φ_d^(I) and its printed ticks run 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.
The front-right horizontal axis is labelled ln Z_p^(I) with printed ticks 22 to 36 in steps of 2.
The front-left horizontal axis is labelled ln Z_p^(II)(ε+Δε) with printed ticks 22 to 36 (drawn 36 down to 22).
The colour bar is labelled k_s(ε+Δε) and its printed ticks are 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1, blue = low, yellow = high.
The bottom plane at φ_d^(I) = 0 is uniformly bright yellow, i.e. k_s = 1 across the whole Z_p range.
Upper planes remain yellow along the diagonal where the two ln Z_p values are equal and become green/blue at corners where the stage-I and stage-II Z_p values differ most.
k_s equals 1 under non-recrystallization (φ_d^(I) = 0), indicating the net change Δσ_s in saturation stress is unaffected by varying conditions.
k_s also equals 1 under constant deformation conditions, i.e. ln Z_p^(I) = ln Z_p^(II)(ε+Δε).
The softening effect on the saturation stress is enhanced, shown as a decline in k_s, with increasing difference between the Z_p of the two stages and rising φ_d^(I).
The caption identifies the two stages of deformation as stage I and stage II and couples k_s to the DRX fraction.

measured_quantities: ln Z_p of stage I and stage II (dimensionless)
